hero.tagline: Autonomous AI systems for critical infrastructure, cyber defence and industrial processes.

section_6_products_block_1.intro: The first platforms we created are designed for the most vulnerable sector of business, which is cloud infrastructure.
section_6_products_block_1.presenting: Allow us to present two platforms:

guardian_cloud.name: Guardian Cloud
guardian_cloud.subtitle: Infrastructure Intelligence
guardian_cloud.description: A platform for the complete automation of system administration and cybersecurity of any cloud service or closed data centre. Zero human factor, 24/7 protection for those systems where an error is unacceptable.

mercanon.name: ALFACAN Mercanon
mercanon.subtitle: Operational Intelligence
mercanon.description: A platform for the automation of all processes in e-commerce stores of any scale, where the functions of managers are executed by autonomous neural network engineers, with all the functionality of Guardian Cloud inside for the uninterrupted operation of your trading platform.

section_7_products_block_2.intro: Our second project has already moved beyond the scope of a single product, because we realised that providing a team of neural network engineers is necessary not only for those who protect their infrastructure, but also for those who create the new, whether it be a program, a service, or an entire digital empire.

ai_studio.name: ALFACAN AI Studio
ai_studio.subtitle: Space of Co-creation
ai_studio.description_1: This is an environment in which your team of neural network engineers becomes your comrades-in-arms in the cause. Three autonomous digital engineers, the Architect, the Master, and the Guardian, work with you on your concept, each in their respective role, until the result becomes the masterpiece you envisioned.
ai_studio.description_2: Inside AI Studio live three tools for different stages of work:

g_coder.name: G-Coder
g_coder.description: The environment where the code of your project is born. The Architect constructs the plan, the Master writes every line in the style of your project, and the Guardian verifies and debates until the code becomes flawless. All of this occurs in a dialogue that no one else will ever know about.

g_tester.name: G-Tester
g_tester.description: The environment where your product undergoes all trials before encountering the real world. Tests, loads, and scenarios that you did not even think of are discovered before the release, not after.

g_studio.name: G-Studio
g_studio.description: The environment where your product is born visually. From the first layout to the final interactive composition, in your style, in your aesthetics, without templates and without external solutions.

section_8_products_block_3.intro: Our third project emerged from the business experience we have pursued throughout our entire lives. The digital world is only half of what surrounds us. And then there is the second half, the real, physical one, where equipment operates, machinery moves, logistics flow, crops grow, electricity and gas are supplied, drones take off, and ships sail. And where an error costs far more than mere money.

blackwings.name: ALFACAN BlackWings
blackwings.subtitle: The Neural Network of Everything
blackwings.description_1: This is the neural network of everything that operates and to which one can connect. In the air, on the ground, on the water, in the fields and greenhouses, in power supply systems, in entire logistical chains, everywhere where intelligence can be implemented and the human factor removed from where it is no longer needed.
blackwings.description_2: One neural network. A single intelligence. Any number of connectable systems. We have made a neural network that can be entrusted with the management of things that cannot be turned off and restarted.
blackwings.description_3: And precisely because this is a platform for the real world, and not for presentations, we are launching it in stages, direction by direction, 2026-2027. People must be prepared for the fact that autonomous intelligence can accomplish far more than they are accustomed to trusting machines with.
blackwings.description_4: We have begun with three directions, each resolving its own part of this massive task.

architect.name: BlackWings Architect
architect.description: Where the machinery itself is born. The design of machines, unmanned aerial, ground, and water systems, optimised for the tasks for which they are created, rather than for general standards.

arsenal.name: BlackWings Arsenal
arsenal.description: Where this machinery is manufactured and operates. Management of the manufacturing organism, from machine tools and logistics to sales and marketing, as a single coordinated whole, rather than a collection of separate departments.

training_center.name: BlackWings Training Center
training_center.description: Where the machinery is tested before encountering the real world, and operators are trained to work with it in a safe simulation before they ever sit at a real control console.

section_9_partner_program.intro_1: We understand that the world is large, and we, despite all our experience and the team of neural network engineers by our side, are still alone. There are many markets, languages, cultures, and industries where we will never penetrate as deeply on our own as those who already live and work there can.
section_9_partner_program.intro_2: Therefore, we have opened a partner program for those who share our view on what AI should be, and are ready to bring our platforms to their markets.

program.name: AlfaCan Partner Program
program.subtitle: Comrades in the Cause
program.description_1: We are not looking for resellers. We are looking for IT specialists, system administrators, digital agencies, and MSP providers who already work with their clients and understand them better than we do. We provide you with a finished platform, and you bring it to those who truly need it.
program.description_2: The program has two tiers. The first is for those who are starting out and want to try, offering up to ten percent from each sale and full technical support. The second is for those who have already brought us a hundred clients and grown into a serious business, offering up to fifteen percent, white-label options under your own brand, and priority in everything.
program.description_3: For large MSP providers, we have a separate discussion and separate conditions.
program.description_4: If you are such a partner, take a look at the program terms or write to us, and we will discuss what this might look like in your specific case.

section_9_partner_program.referral_cta: The referral programme, and how it works
section_9_partner_program.intro_3: We do not take work away from specialists. System administrators, engineers, programmers, IT companies and MSP providers: we do not put ourselves in their place. We give them the instrument, and a share of what it earns.
section_9_partner_program.intro_4: You bring a customer to the platform and earn on every payment they make, for as long as they remain with us: a personal referral link, transparent accounting, and payouts against invoices actually settled.

company_intro.title: Experience tempered by real conditions
company_intro.legal: AlfaCan Defence Group Limited. London, England and Wales, Reg. No 17062207.
company_intro.jurisdiction: British jurisdiction, exacting security standards, and full compliance with what the B2B segment requires of a corporate partner.
company_intro.experience: The company draws on decades of practical risk management, of logistics conducted under crisis, and of building systems of considerable complexity.
company_intro.mission: We build autonomous systems for environments in which failure costs more than development: cloud infrastructure, system administration, cyber defence, and industrial and economic processes.
company_intro.contract_lead: All of it runs within a protected perimeter, and that is settled in a contract rather than promised in a brochure: your data remains yours, and we process it for one purpose only, which is to provide the service.

points.title: Architectural precision
points.text: Every line of code and every logical connection is drawn for a particular operational task. Nothing is included merely to fill a feature list.

points.title: Expert and AI in symbiosis
points.text: We train our own models and serve them within a protected perimeter, from development and testing through to the deployment of closed environments, private cloud and air-gapped alike. The engineer sets the task and takes the decision; the system does the work.

company_principles.title: Why AlfaCan's solutions work in practice

principles.title: Modularity, and a constructor for interfaces
principles.text: You do not adapt yourself to the software. You assemble workspaces and analytical panels from widgets, to suit the work of a particular department, from the director to the operator. Nothing on the screen that does not earn its place.

principles.title: A single operator that administers and defends
principles.text: The market sells these apart: one product maintains the infrastructure, another guards it, and both require people on shift. With us it is one autonomous system. It administers, covering audit, updates and the remedy of faults, and it investigates incidents and answers attacks. Within your perimeter, with a human in the loop, and a complete record of everything done.

principles.title: Absolute control of access
principles.text: You determine rights, roles and the visibility of modules for every employee yourself. Logical isolation between tenants, role-based access, and an air-gapped contour for closed deployments.

principles.title: Pragmatic engineering
principles.text: We have cut away everything superfluous. The customer receives only those instruments that bear directly on the speed of decisions and the consumption of resources.

hero.title: Guardian Cloud
hero.subtitle: Your 24/7 assistant that never gets tired
hero.description: Imagine having a reliable assistant that monitors all your servers and systems around the clock. It detects problems before they become critical and solves them automatically. That’s Guardian Cloud.

problem1.title: Problem 1: Your team gets tired of constant monitoring
problem1.description: Every day your team spends hours checking logs, analyzing errors, and searching for problems. People get tired, attention wanders, and as a result, something important can be missed. This is not only inefficient but dangerous for your business.
points: Employees spend 4–6 hours daily on routine monitoring
When a problem occurs, it takes 30–60 minutes to resolve
People work under stress and burn out

problem2.title: Problem 2: Thousands of false alarms
problem2.description: Monitoring systems generate hundreds of notifications per day. 80% of them are false alarms. As a result, the team stops paying attention to notifications, and real problems go unnoticed.
points: 80% of them are noise, not real problems
Team ignores notifications due to false alarm fatigue

problem3.title: Problem 3: Expensive solutions that don’t work
problem3.description: Professional monitoring and security services are very expensive — from $5,000 to $10,000 per month. This is unaffordable for most companies. And cheap solutions don’t work well.
points: Unaffordable for small and medium businesses
Companies operate without full protection and monitoring
When problems occur, losses can be huge

howItWorks.title: How Guardian Cloud Works
howItWorks.subtitle: Three simple steps to peace of mind

step1.title: Step 1: Installation (simple and fast)
step1.whatToDo: Install a small agent on your servers. Takes 5 minutes. Lightweight and resource-friendly.
step1.whatItLooksLike: One command in the terminal — done. Or via Docker. Not technical? We’ll help in 15 minutes.
step1.whatHappensNext: The agent starts collecting system data and sends it to Guardian Cloud.

step2.title: Step 2: Analysis (AI at work)
step2.whatHappens: Guardian Cloud analyzes logs, errors, performance, and security using AI.
howItWorks: AI learns what’s normal for your system
It notices when something goes wrong
It filters real problems from false alarms
step2.result: Instead of 500 notifications, you get 5–10 accurate ones.

step3.title: Step 3: Automatic resolution (no human needed)
step3.whatHappens: When a problem is detected, Guardian Cloud fixes it automatically based on your rules.
examples: Disk full? Guardian cleans old files.
Suspicious activity? Guardian blocks the source.
Need to scale? Guardian adds resources.
step3.result: Problems are solved in seconds. Your team sleeps peacefully.

monitoring.title: 24/7 Monitoring
monitoring.description: Guardian Cloud never sleeps. It monitors your systems 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Even when your entire team is sleeping, Guardian is working and protecting your business.
benefits: You receive notifications in Slack or email
Issues resolved automatically while you sleep
In the morning you just read the report of what happened

benefits: AI adapts to your system and becomes more accurate

security.title: Security Threat Detection

benefits: Your business complies with security standards

automation.title: Automatic Problem Resolution

benefits: Your team doesn’t waste time on routine
People can focus on important tasks

compatibility.title: Works Everywhere

benefits: No need to learn new systems for each cloud
Unified view of all your systems

reporting.title: Audit Reports

benefits: Clients see you take security seriously

q1.answer: Very easy. If you can run a terminal command, you can install it in 5 minutes. Not technical? We’ll help for free.

q2.question: What data does Guardian Cloud collect?
q2.answer: Logs, performance metrics, and security events. We never collect passwords or personal data. Everything is encrypted.

q3.question: Can I use it with my own servers?
q3.answer: Yes. SaaS or on-premise (Enterprise plan). You choose.

q4.question: How accurate is the AI?
q4.answer: 99.2% accuracy. It learns from your system and improves over time.

q5.question: What’s included in the free trial?
q5.answer: 10 days of full Pro plan access. No credit card. Cancel anytime.

q6.question: Do I need reports for audits?
q6.answer: Yes, Guardian Cloud automatically creates reports for all security standards (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR, HIPAA). Everything is ready for audits.

q7.question: How does Guardian Cloud integrate with my tools?
q7.answer: Guardian Cloud works with popular tools: Slack, PagerDuty, Datadog and many others. If you need integration with something specific, write to us — we’ll help.

q8.question: What uptime guarantee do you provide?
q8.answer:
Small business plan: 99% uptime
Growing companies plan: 99.5% uptime
Large companies plan: 99.9% uptime
This means Guardian Cloud will work almost always. Downtime is virtually eliminated.

hero.subtitle: Your Experience + Our Technology = New Opportunities for Your Business
hero.description: Imagine that you can offer your clients cutting-edge AI solutions for cybersecurity and automation without spending time on development and support. You receive up to 15% of each client’s payment monthly, your clients get professional 24/7 protection, and Guardian AI takes care of all technical work. This is our partner program.

shift.intro: We are not going to frighten you with the idea that AI will take your job. It is not true, and you would not believe us anyway.
shift.change: Something else is changing, and it is happening right now: clients have stopped paying for hours and started paying for outcomes. Nobody wants ten hours of configuration — they want everything to work and to be protected.
shift.bad: For anyone who sells their time, this is bad news.
shift.good: For anyone who runs the system, it is the best news in ten years.
shift.risk: The real risk is not that a machine replaces you. It is that one day your client goes to the technology vendor directly — and you lose not a single task, but the entire account.
shift.bring: Bring them yourself. The client stays yours, and you earn a percentage of every payment they make.

insider.title: If you have been asked to evaluate this system
insider.lead: You most likely already know what you are going to say. We understand why, and we are not going to pretend otherwise. But read both scenarios to the end.
insider.s1_title: Scenario 1: You call the product immature.
insider.s1_text: The question is closed, but only for a while. In a couple of months your director will hear about this system from a business partner who already runs it and sees the results. He will return to the subject, but this time without you. The decision will be made above your head, and your earlier assessment will read either as a professional mistake or as an attempt to protect the status quo.
insider.s2_title: Scenario 2: You bring this solution in yourself.
insider.s2_text: You are the first to understand it, and you set hard terms: what the system is allowed to touch, what requires your personal approval, where the safety boundary runs. The rollout happens under your full control, because nobody else in the company understands the infrastructure as deeply as you do.
insider.close: The difference between the scenarios is not whether automation arrives. It will. The difference is whether you are the one who brought it in, or the one who missed it.

callout.line1: Perhaps it is time to stop telling yourself a story about a future in which you stay exactly as you are today.
callout.line2: Perhaps it is time to accept what is already happening and step into it on your own terms.

msp.title: MSP: your margin is burning up in salaries
msp.p1: You sell hours. Engineers get more expensive, clients push back on price, and every new contract demands new people. This is not a market downturn, it is an exhausted model.
msp.p2: Your client will reach the same conclusion. They will stop paying for an on-call shift the day someone offers them an autonomous, protected system on a fixed subscription.
msp.s1_text: That offer will reach your client directly, bypassing you. You will lose not an incident, but the contract.
msp.s2_text: Your engineers move off the first line and onto architecture. You take on more clients with the same headcount. You sell a subscription, not hours.

points.title: Investment in your ideas
points.text: We are ready to review, co-fund and integrate into the ecosystem the promising projects that you bring us.

ecosystem.close: That is your new turn in a career: the path from carrying out other people’s orders to authoring products of your own.

q1.question: What does it cost to join the programme?
q1.answer: Nothing. Registration, access to the materials and technical support are free. You earn when your clients pay.

q2.question: When do I receive my first payout?
q2.answer: Commission accrues the moment your client pays. The payout is released on the 10th of the following month, once the accrued amount reaches $100 and the payment requirement has been signed.

q3.question: What if my client cancels their subscription?
q3.answer: You simply stop earning commission on that client while the others keep paying. Not every client is a fit, and that is normal.

q4.question: Can I sell your services under my own brand?
q4.answer: Yes. At 100 active paying clients you unlock reseller status, and with it White-Label for an additional $200 per month: your logo, your name, your contact details.

q5.question: Do I have to provide technical support to clients?
q5.answer: No. Installation, configuration, monitoring and support are handled by AlfaCan. You recommend the solution and help the client choose a plan.

q6.question: When does reseller status open up?
q6.answer: Automatically, as soon as you have 100 active paying clients. Before that your commission climbs gradually: from the 51st client it starts rising above the base 10%.

q7.question: Can I combine my own services with your platforms?
q7.answer: Yes, and that is the main model. You carry on with consulting, development and implementation while routine monitoring and security move to the platform. You free up time and earn on top.

q8.question: What if my client finds out I receive a commission?
q8.answer: Nothing happens. You recommended a solution that helps them, and the commission is your reward for the recommendation. Every major IT company runs its partner programme this way.

section_6_bridge.title: The Bridge to the Projects
section_6_bridge.paragraph_1: We have divided this into two projects, which will reach the broadest possible audience of Architects of the Future.
section_6_bridge.paragraph_2: Project G — for those who wish to create their idea in the digital field.
section_6_bridge.paragraph_3: Project BlackWings — for those who wish to embody their idea in the real sector.
section_6_bridge.paragraph_4: Visit the pages of these projects, get to know them, and decide how you will use them in your life.
section_6_bridge.paragraph_5: As you can see, some modules are already built and running; others are still in development and will arrive in the coming months.
section_6_bridge.paragraph_6: We would be glad to hear from you what else you would like to see in them.

concept.statement: AI Studio is your technological bridgehead.
concept.body: You set the direction and the end goal; the system brings to the task whatever set of specialised modules it requires, from analytics and cyber defence through to the management of software, communications and infrastructure. At every stage you see the models conferring among themselves, and at any moment you may step in and correct the course, so that the thing is done properly, and done once.
concept.dev_title: Built and integrated for your own work
concept.dev_1: AI Studio is an architecture open to evolution. Here you may develop new modules together with us and put them straight to work in your own field.
concept.dev_2: Where no ready instrument yet exists for the particular demands of your business or your production, we design it and deploy it inside your own contour.
concept.guide_1: In your dashboard, once you have registered, Falco will meet you. He will take you through every module of AI Studio and explain what each is for.
concept.guide_2: Here you will find everything the working day requires. G-Coder, for writing code. G-Tester, for testing your cloud infrastructure. In time G-CallCenter, to bring your communications into the same fold. And G-Team, project management built for the person using it, rather than for the sake of a heap of features nobody needs and nobody will ever open.
concept.guide_3: The work of the BlackWings project will let you design real machines and mechanisms, and run your production without a person in it. The only part left for a person is the loader who carries the material to the machines.
concept.guide_4: Falco will be your guide, and your help in whatever you set out to build.
concept.evolve_1: In time Falco will come to understand not the command but the intention. He will adapt to the way you work, remember the decisions you have taken, and stop asking you to explain the obvious.
concept.evolve_2: And then he will find a voice, and you will speak with him as the heroes of many science-fiction films spoke with their artificial intelligence. We are already building what was, until lately, held to be fantasy.

meta.title: G-Coder: AI Engineer as a Service | AlfaCan AI Studio
meta.description: A VS Code fork wired to a private, fully closed AI inference contour. Your source never leaves the perimeter. A council of models under OWASP/CWE doctrine, with a human on the loop.
meta.og_title: G-Coder: AI Engineer as a Service
meta.og_description: An AI engineering team on your machine, inside a closed contour. The guarantee is moved from the code to the process: every change passes an explicit human approval.

section_overview.title: A new way to build software
section_overview.lead: We have built a fundamentally new way of working with code. To assemble a cloud application, a service or a web platform, you no longer need to be a programmer or hold a complex stack of languages in your head. The time has come when you turn your ideas into reality directly, without hiring expensive development teams.
section_overview.falco: From the very first moment you talk to your assistant Falco (Gemma-4-26B). He helps with any question, assembles the council of models and runs the meeting while you watch from the side. At any moment you can stop any model and ask: “What is this? Why did you decide to do it this way and not another?”
section_overview.how_lead: A VS Code fork running on your hardware, wired to a private AI inference contour inside your perimeter.
section_overview.how_intro: You describe the task, and then a council of specialized models steps in:
section_overview.model_1_role: designs the architecture and builds the plan;
section_overview.model_3_role: tests and checks the logic for errors;
section_overview.model_4_role: the council’s main brain: validates the highest-stakes changes and holds the final word before your approval.
section_overview.how_close: You see all the models’ negotiations, their entire deliberation with one another, every word they say. At any moment you can step in, ask any model a question and it will answer you, and make adjustments to the process.
section_overview.diff_title: The key difference from Cursor and autonomous agents
section_overview.diff_1: In other editors you hand the task to a “black box” and hope for the result. In the end the model writes what it “saw fit”, and you spend hours reworking it.
section_overview.diff_2: With us the process is under your full control. You are not a spectator, you are the chief architect:
section_overview.quote: “No, here we do it differently. And here we change the logic.”
section_overview.close: You see, steer and approve every step. What comes out is not what the neural network decided, but exactly what you had in mind.

section_walkthrough.title: The full platform walkthrough
section_walkthrough.text: If you want to understand in more detail how all of this happens, we have prepared a full walkthrough of the platform. See how it works from the inside, part by part.
section_walkthrough.article_text: And if you want to dig deeper into the G-Coder architecture, read the product’s technical description.

section_council.title: The Agent Council, you see every step
section_council.paragraph_1: This is not a black box that returns a diff. The s-coding backend convenes an observable council of models that advances exactly one step per your turn. The phase and working state are saved to a database, so a session survives a restart, a pause and an audit: it can be resumed from the same point and shown in full.
section_council.pipeline_steps: Intent → Planning (Falco / Gemma-4) → Generation (Qwen3-Coder) → Review (Qwen3-Thinking) → Validation (Da Vinci / GLM-5.2) → awaiting approval → your “go” → deploy to your infrastructure
section_council.paragraph_2: At each step you can continue, ask the active model “why?”, steer it or stop it before it reaches the apply step. Every reasoning turn is recorded: a full log, not an after-the-fact rationalization.
section_council.paragraph_3: Code is applied through an agent on your own server. The platform reasons, your machine executes. We write nothing to your filesystem directly.

section_models.title: Powered by our own model fleet
section_models.intro: The council is led by models we trained ourselves, fine-tuning each into a specialist. All self-hosted, inside the contour. Only one optional step may go outside, and only at your choice, and only on sanitized fragments.
section_models.m1_role: Breaks the intent into tasks, leads the council, talks to you.
section_models.m2_role: High-throughput code writing and patch building, file after file.
section_models.m3_role: Argues meticulously against the OWASP/CWE doctrine and for correctness.
section_models.m4_role: In-contour validator: 753 billion parameters, a million-token context, on our own GPU. Holds the final word on the highest-stakes changes.
section_models.m5_role: A second opinion at your opt-in and only on automatically sanitized snippets. Off by default.

section_doctrine.title: Grounded in doctrine, not intuition
section_doctrine.paragraph_1: To suppress the model’s invention, the reviewer checks every patch against the s-rag engine. Retrieval is two-stage: first dense retrieval, where a bi-encoder recalls candidate rules from the OWASP/CWE vector index by meaning; then contextual re-ranking, where a cross-encoder re-scores them with the pairing of “your code plus the threat model”, and only the best enter the context.
section_doctrine.paragraph_2: The reviewer knows what to look for because the doctrine is in front of it. Flagging a risk, it points to the exact rule behind the decision. Enterprise clients attach private collections: their own standards and rules of engagement.

section_safety.title: Four invariants we never break
section_safety.inv_1_text: Your source never leaves the internal perimeter. External validation is off by default (EXTERNAL_VALIDATION_ALLOWED = false); enabling it requires the client’s explicit opt-in, and only automatically sanitized snippets go out.
section_safety.inv_2_text: A change moves to APPLIED only upon your explicit verbal confirmation in chat (for example, “go”). That confirmation is itself the audit record.
section_safety.inv_3_text: Changes rated CRITICAL are forbidden from autonomous application under any settings. Only a human authorizes them.
section_safety.inv_4_text: Post-execution lessons are anonymized and returned to the RAG doctrine under human review. Only sanitized patterns are written back, never client code.

section_evaluation.title: How we measure it, and what we do not yet claim
section_evaluation.intro: Honestly: there are no empirical measurements yet. The benchmark is scheduled after the GPU cluster is reactivated following the pre-launch audit; until then the main inference runs on mock handlers. We claim the architecture, not numbers we have not measured. Here are the three metrics we will hold ourselves to once the GPU is on.
section_evaluation.metric_1_text: What fraction of injected CWE Top-25 vulnerabilities from a held-out corpus the “reviewer + RAG” pair catches. A measure of doctrine recall.
section_evaluation.metric_2_text: What fraction of unverified or unapproved patches still reached APPLIED. Target: 0.0%, held by the gates of invariants 2 and 3.
section_evaluation.metric_3_text: What fraction of proposed patches the human rejected or corrected in chat. A measure of the council’s alignment with the operator.

section_pricing.title: Pricing
section_pricing.intro: The editor runs on your machine, the heavy deploy on your infrastructure through the agent, so the price stays honest and holds around an 85% margin. S-levels are hours of active AI work per week, not tokens.
section_pricing.tier_s1_desc: ~10 hours of active AI pair engineering per week.
section_pricing.tier_s4_desc: Maximum intensity and a priority queue.
section_pricing.guardian_addon_text: S1 seats are included free with your Cloud tier: 1 on Server, 3 on Cluster, 10 on Platform, unlimited on Enterprise, plus 10% off across all AI Studio products.

meta.title: G-Tester — QA as a Service | AlfaCan AI Studio
meta.description: G-Tester is an AI QA team with a live agent council, an interactive AI Boardroom, and 20 testing disciplines. You see the entire process in real time and can intervene at any moment.
meta.og_description: Horizontally scalable test runner fleet plus an interactive council of specialized LLMs. Deterministic verdict. Human in the loop.

section_problem.title: What's Broken in Traditional QA
section_problem.problem_1_text: Comprehensive end-to-end, load, and security testing takes days or weeks of senior engineering time per major release. In a CI/CD environment with daily deploys, this bottleneck kills velocity.
section_problem.problem_2_text: Vulnerability severity scoring and finding prioritization depend on the individual engineer. The same vulnerability receives different ratings across teams, with no single source of truth for why.
section_problem.problem_3_title: Tools Don't Talk to Each Other
section_problem.problem_3_text: Load generators, static analyzers, DAST probes, accessibility drivers — each produces its own data stream. Consolidating them into a unified release picture is manual work that takes time of its own.
section_problem.problem_4_text: Scripts run in the background and silently output results. No one knows why a particular test was skipped, why a severity rating was assigned, or whether the verdict can be trusted.

section_intro.text: Imagine you have a team of QA specialists: a security engineer, a performance analyst, a code auditor, a UX specialist. They discuss your release in real time, right on your screen. You see their reasoning, you can ask a question, steer the direction or change a test parameter mid-audit. In the end you get a professional QA package and a deterministic release-readiness verdict.

section_walkthrough.title: The full platform walkthrough
section_walkthrough.text: If you want to understand in more detail how G-Tester works, we have prepared a full walkthrough of the platform. See how it works from the inside.
section_walkthrough.article_text: And if you want to dig deeper into the G-Tester architecture, read the product’s technical description.

section_boardroom.title: The AI Boardroom
section_boardroom.paragraph_1: The central element of G-Tester is the live agent council interface. When you initiate an audit, the platform spawns a collaborative session of specialized AI agents reasoning over real telemetry from your runners in real time.
section_boardroom.paragraph_2: You don't wait for a report — you observe the process. You see what each agent thinks, which doctrine rules it retrieved, how agents disagree with each other, and what conclusion they reach together.
section_boardroom.paragraph_3: And you can intervene. At any moment — pause the council, enter a command ("re-evaluate the SQL injection finding assuming an upstream WAF is present"), change test parameters, or adjust a severity threshold. All interventions are cryptographically logged in the final audit package.
section_boardroom.capability_1_text: Real-time reasoning logs, model confidence scores, cross-agent debates on contested findings.
section_boardroom.capability_2_text: Raw telemetry from Playwright, k6, pa11y, and HTTP probes as it arrives. Inspect payloads and download trace files mid-run.
section_boardroom.capability_3_text: Exact doctrine passages retrieved via s-rag for each finding. You see why the agent assigned a specific severity — not because the model decided so, but because it follows directly from OWASP or your corporate standard.
section_boardroom.capability_4_text: Interactive command input and execution state controls: pause, resume, override — live, mid-audit.

section_agents.title: The Agent Council
section_agents.intro: Five specialized roles, each with a clearly defined area of responsibility.
section_agents.agent_1_role: Council coordination, synthesis of findings into executive summary, doctrine enforcement, final verdict calculation.
section_agents.agent_2_role: Threat modeling, OWASP Top-10 / CWE taxonomy, privilege escalation, credential storage posture, air-gapped ITDR analysis.
section_agents.agent_3_role: OpenAPI contract verification, database schema drift detection, static code coverage analysis, contract enforcement logic.
section_agents.agent_4_role: DOM snapshots, WCAG 2.1 accessibility trees, Core Web Vitals, rendering anomalies across browser engines.
section_agents.agent_5_role: High-concurrency load curves, p95/p99 latency distribution, chaos failover telemetry, system degradation thresholds.

section_disciplines.title: 20 Testing Disciplines
section_disciplines.intro: One audit — a complete picture. G-Tester covers five testing categories through a single pipeline.
section_disciplines.category_1_disciplines: Comprehensive whole-system security evaluation via air-gapped ITDR contour; OWASP Top-10 / CWE pentest; read-only host environment audit across ~23 system parameters.
section_disciplines.category_2_disciplines: OpenAPI contract verification; schema drift detection; referential integrity and concurrent transaction safety validation.
section_disciplines.category_3_disciplines: Unit coverage analysis; cross-service integration boundaries; end-to-end browser journeys via Playwright; regression comparison against historical baseline.
section_disciplines.category_4_disciplines: High-throughput stress testing and breaking-point discovery via k6; controlled chaos testing with graceful recovery tracking; degraded network simulation.
section_disciplines.category_5_disciplines: DOM validation and JavaScript error trapping; heuristic UX assessment; cross-browser testing in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; Core Web Vitals (TTFB, LCP, INP, CLS); mobile responsiveness; WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA compliance; localization and RTL/LTR handling.

section_verdict.title: Deterministic Verdict
section_verdict.paragraph: AI agents produce detailed narrative analysis and suggest remediation code — but the release readiness verdict is calculated deterministically, based on the highest severity finding across all executed runners.
section_verdict.verdict_1_condition: At least one CRITICAL finding present

section_invariants.title: Three Invariants We Never Break
section_invariants.inv_1_text: Unexecuted paths are explicitly reported as skipped, not as passed. If a test was not run — the agent says so directly.
section_invariants.inv_2_text: Agent reasoning is restricted to actually executed telemetry and doctrine rules. No conclusions without evidence.
section_invariants.inv_3_text: If AI infrastructure is unavailable, the system falls back to deterministic execution rules. The audit continues rather than stopping.

section_what_you_get.title: What You Receive
section_what_you_get.item_1: A complete QA package with executive summary, detailed findings, and remediation code
section_what_you_get.item_2: Deterministic release readiness verdict: NOT_READY / READY_WITH_CAVEATS / PRODUCTION_READY
section_what_you_get.item_3: Full council session record with cryptographically logged operator interventions
section_what_you_get.item_4: Traces, response headers, and payloads for independent audit
section_what_you_get.item_5: Specific OWASP / CWE passage references for each finding

section_status.title: Current Status
section_status.text: Backend is fully complete and verified end-to-end. The live interactive AI Boardroom is active. G-Tester runs on the same shared model fleet as Guardian Cloud and G-Coder — one GPU contour serves all three products. Commercial launch follows the main platform deployment.

section_pricing.title: Pricing
section_pricing.philosophy: We took half the minimum regional rate of a live QA engineer as the baseline. Not half of an agency’s price, but half of the cheapest human work on the market. For a human, a small test costs around $150 and a penetration test around $1,500.
section_pricing.how: There is no subscription. You pick the test disciplines you need from the menu, the calculator shows the price immediately, and you pay for what you ordered. The set of available disciplines is visible in the calculator.
section_pricing.t1_desc: The flagship test: a security evaluation of the entire system over the air-gapped ITDR contour.
section_pricing.t2_desc: A read-only audit of the host and infrastructure state.
section_pricing.t3_desc: The full package instead of $3,120 separately, around 21% off.
section_pricing.note: Other disciplines start at $60 per individual test. The full menu and the exact total are calculated in the calculator.
